text: It’s a great TV. I have one in my living room (not sure if it’s an F, but S95 from last year). But, my primary use is on my desk, I have 2 55” TVs as my monitors, and I’m not very comfortable with using OLEDs there. They can be on for basically the entire day with a lot of static images. RGB mini LED works better as I don’t have to worry about burn in, and TBH I like the image more than S95. It’s brighter with more intense colors (but without over saturation like Samsung tends to do). It’s still an LED backlight, so black won’t be as perfect as on OLED, but much better than QN95-whatever that I had before (that one was had an IPS panel, so off-axis glow was pretty bad), and it’s not noticeable unless it’s like a small text in black background. The only problem is size, 65” is too big (very immersive for games/movies/calls, but not great for work), but that’s just for my scenario. Hopefully they’ll shrink the tech for next generation.

text: I don't think it's necessarily strange for people to not like this approach to data management and as I mentioned in my post, there is a way for you to have your cake and eat it too with other software. It's not a "complaint" as much as just dissatisfaction with the way it currently works and for those that feel that way, they look to find other tools to do the job the way they want it to. Furthermore, by providing feedback to the Immich team, they quickly rolled out storage templates as the default, which is a net positive change I believe, so highlighting this stuff does have a purpose beyond just yelling into the internet void.
